intro.title: Build feature flag utility with variants
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple feature flag utility that allows you to toggle different versions (variants) of a feature in your JavaScript application. You'll learn how to use objects to store configuration data and conditional logic to control which variant is active. The main technologies involved are JavaScript objects, conditional statements (if/else), and functions. By the end, you'll have a reusable utility that can help manage feature rollouts or A/B testing in your projects.
intro.usecase: Feature flags with variants are used by companies like Netflix and Amazon to test different UI designs before full rollout. Developers implement them in dashboards to toggle between chart layouts or data visualizations, and in e-commerce product pages to A/B test button colors or placement. This pattern allows gradual feature releases, enabling teams to measure performance impact and roll back changes instantly if issues arise.
